# tablekit

> Glue and instrumentation for running a tabletop game where some of the seats
> are AI agents. One append-only JSONL per session serves as both the play
> ledger (in the shape dmcheck reads) and a five-lane telemetry stream. Exit
> codes: 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 refused. Stdlib only, no network in the
> analysis path, MIT.

Use tablekit when an agent or a human needs to: run a hybrid table over a chat
platform without cues silently failing to deliver; know mid-session whether a
seat has been left out, a roll went unconsumed, or an engine event was never
narrated; and afterwards, learn what the evening was actually like from each
seat rather than from the transcript alone.

## The governing rule: the table speaks English

There are no chat commands, no token vocabulary, no keywords for players to
learn. Text RPGs handed players verb lists because 1980s parsers could not
understand a sentence; that workaround is why they feel like operating a
computer rather than sitting with a person running a world. An agent GM that
reintroduces it throws away its only advantage over a parser game. Whatever
someone types in the channel is dialogue. This is a product non-goal enforced
by tests, not a preference.

## Install

- `pip install tablekit`, then `tablekit init`.
- `python3 examples/demo_session.py` runs a whole synthetic session and prints
  its report with no configuration and no network.

## The lanes

- `qa` - delivery, latency, listener uptime, command failures. Automatic.
- `qc` - refereeing checks, split into defects (boundary crossings, pass/fail)
  and attention items (dosage readings). Automatic.
- `ux` - participation and waiting, derived from the record. No scoring.
- `uxr` - what the evening was like from each seat. Captured two ways, both in
  plain English: inferred during play from what people already said (six
  internal buckets - pacing, floor, comprehension, resonance, spotlight,
  continuity - never shown to the table), and asked about conversationally at
  the close. The close-out questions are the structural check on the first
  half, because a GM that did not notice friction cannot have recorded it.
- `out` - outcome pairs recording an intent and its later payoff (cue taken,
  roll consumed, quiet seat returned), the only way to ask whether a craft move
  worked.

## Contracts

- The table is never given a syntax to learn.
- An inferred signal is advisory in every path and can never become a defect.
- Every inferred signal stores the speaker's own words, so the inference is
  auditable by whoever was in the room.
- Below three occurrences, individual moments are listed and no rate is stated.
- No composite score is produced anywhere.
- Player prose is not stored unless you ask for it with --keep-text.
- A source-native message ID is receipted before routing and deduplicates every
  replay, including quarantine. Missing IDs cannot resolve state.
- One inbound/result closes at most one typed obligation, and only with an
  explicit correlation to that compatible open pair. Missing correlation,
  blank input, and invalid correlation close none and remain visible.
- Identity fallback is exact after Unicode/case/whitespace normalization;
  unknown remains unknown and substring matching is forbidden.
- Free-form roll prose is advisory only. A verified, exactly attributed,
  structurally valid relay result may resolve a roll only when it also carries
  an explicit pair correlation.
- Pair IDs are collision-resistant; duplicate opens, orphan/second closes,
  kind changes, and invalid kind-specific outcomes are refused.

## Related

srdcheck (rules verdicts), charactercheck (sheet derivation), dmcheck (table
conduct - reads this kit's session file with no export step).
